title: Foot compression for improvement of walking ability of patients with claudicatio intermittens
summary:
LEAD is a common disease that primarily affects the blood vessels in the lower extremities. Atherosclerotic changes with narrowing or blockages of the leg arteries reduce blood flow, resulting in less blood reaching the leg muscles and less oxygen and nutrients being supplied to them, which leads to reduced functionality, strength, and walking distance. 
The reduced blood flow to the legs with the consequences described above is followed by typical symptoms such as pain and weakness in the legs, especially during physical activity, as typical signs of an insufficient supply of oxygen and nutrients. In critical stages of LEAD, pain can also occur at rest.
The treatment of LEAD varies depending on the stage of the disease. For patients with intermittent claudication, exercise training is recommended to improve walking distance. If the condition worsens, interventional revascularization is considered. 
Recent studies have shown that intermittent pneumatic compression (IPC) improves blood circulation in the legs and increases walking distance. This therapy can be used in addition to training or as an alternative when other therapies are not possible. However, there is currently no standard regarding the type of device, cycle sequence, and frequency or duration of IPC application.
The VADOplex medical device is used for IPC on the foot. VADOplex is designed to improve venous return through intermittent pneumatic impulse compression on the lower extremities. The rapid build-up of pressure in the VADOplex cuff leads to rapid emptying of the venous plexus in the foot and increased venous return flow. This ultimately leads to relaxation of the vascular muscles and vasodilation. As a result, the arteries can be better supplied with blood and the muscles become more efficient again, with little or no pain in the legs. 
For a total of 6 months, patients should use VADOplex on their feet for at least 4 hours per day, including at least one hour at a time, in addition to the normal recommended walking training of at least 30-60 minutes 3 times per week. The additional IPC should lead to an improvement in the (pain-free) walking distance and a corresponding improvement in quality of life.

interventions.name: VADOplex application for at least 4 hours per day and at least one hour duration at a single time point combined with independent walking training (standard of care therapy (SOC)) as recommended with performance of walking training at least 3 times a week for 30-60 minutes per session for a 6 months
Independent walking training (SOC therapy) as recommended at least 3 times a week for 30-60 minutes per session for a 6 months period in total.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-	Adequate general condition, clinical stability (not frail, without pronounced overweight or underweight)
-	Sufficient cognitive function and compliance
-	Sufficient mobility in the home environment
-	Ability to participate at the control visits or to be transported to preliminary and follow-up visits.
-	Best medical treatment under stable conditions for at least three months before study inclusion.
Exclusion criteria:
-	Manifested venous or lymphatic edema
-	Surgical revascularization or other interventions within the last 3 months,
-	Planned surgical revascularization during the intervention period (6 months)
-	Existing wounds at the lower extremities
-	New RAS acting agents during participation in the registry trial
-	Post-stroke condition with residual cognitive, sensory or motor deficits, cerebrovascular events (hemorrhage, TIA, stroke, embolism <30d)
-	Neurological/ neuromuscular underlying diseases (e.g. Parkinson's disease)
-	Underlying psychiatric illnesses (dementia or other cognitive impairments)
-	Mobility-limiting orthopedic or other diseases
-	Cardiovascular diseases including decompensated heart failure, severe aortic valve stenosis and other severe end-stage cardiovascular disease 
-	Cancer with metastatic cancer or life expectance less than 6 months
